cues.en: I have the best job in the world. I'm a doctor. No. Believe me. That's not why. I'm an obesity doctor.
cues.zh: 我拥有世界上最棒的工作。我是一名医生。不，相信我，原因不是这个。我是一名肥胖症医生。

cues.en: I have the honor of working with a group of people subject to the last widely accepted prejudice,
cues.zh: 我有幸与一群人共事，他们承受着最后一种仍被广泛接受的偏见，

cues.en: being fat.
cues.zh: 那就是肥胖。

cues.en: These people have suffered a lot by the time they see me. Shame,
cues.zh: 这些人在来找我之前已经受了很多苦。羞耻、

cues.en: guilt, blame,
cues.zh: 内疚、自责，

cues.en: and outright discrimination.
cues.zh: 还有赤裸裸的歧视。

cues.en: The attitude that many take, including those in health care, is that these people are to blame for their situation.
cues.zh: 许多人——包括医疗行业的人——的态度是，这些人落得如此境地是咎由自取。

cues.en: If they could just control themselves, they wouldn't be overweight,
cues.zh: 只要他们能管住自己，就不会超重，

cues.en: and they're not motivated to change.
cues.zh: 他们只是没有动力去改变。

cues.en: Please let me tell you, this is not the case. The blame, if we've got to extend some here, has been with our advice, and it's time we change that.
cues.zh: 请听我说，事实并非如此。如果非要追究责任，那问题出在我们的建议上，是时候改变了。

cues.en: Obesity is a disease. It's not something created by lack of character.
cues.zh: 肥胖是一种疾病，不是缺乏意志力造成的。

cues.en: It's a hormonal disease,
cues.zh: 它是一种激素类疾病，

cues.en: and there are many hormones involved.
cues.zh: 涉及多种激素。

cues.en: And one of the main ones is a hormone called insulin.
cues.zh: 其中主要的一种叫做胰岛素。

cues.en: Most obese individuals are resistant to this hormone insulin.
cues.zh: 大多数肥胖症患者对胰岛素这种激素存在抵抗。

cues.en: So what does that mean exactly, to be resistant to insulin?
cues.zh: 那么，胰岛素抵抗到底是什么意思呢？

cues.en: Well, insulin resistance is essentially a state of pre pre type two diabetes.
cues.zh: 其实，胰岛素抵抗本质上就是二型糖尿病的前期状态。

cues.en: Insulin's job is to drive glucose or blood sugar into the cells where it can be used.
cues.zh: 胰岛素的职责是把葡萄糖，也就是血糖，送进细胞里供其使用。

cues.en: In a nutshell, when someone is insulin resistant,
cues.zh: 简单来说，当一个人有胰岛素抵抗时，

cues.en: they are having trouble getting blood sugar where it needs to go into those cells,
cues.zh: 他们就难以把血糖送到该去的地方——细胞里，

cues.en: And it just can't hang out in the blood after we eat, or we would all have a diabetic crisis after every meal.
cues.zh: 而血糖不能在进食后一直待在血液里，否则我们每顿饭后都会发生糖尿病危象。

cues.en: So when someone is resistant to insulin, the body's response to this is to just make more of it, and insulin levels will rise and rise.
cues.zh: 当一个人出现胰岛素抵抗时，身体的反应就是制造更多胰岛素，胰岛素水平会一路升高。

cues.en: And for a while, years even, this is gonna keep up, and blood sugar levels can remain normal.
cues.zh: 在一段时间内，甚至好几年里，身体还能撑住，血糖水平可以保持正常。

cues.en: However, usually, it can't keep up forever.
cues.zh: 然而，通常它不可能永远撑下去。

cues.en: And even at those elevated
cues.zh: 甚至在这些升高的

cues.en: levels of insulin are not enough to keep blood sugar in the normal range.
cues.zh: 胰岛素水平下，也不足以把血糖维持在正常范围内。

cues.en: So it starts to rise.
cues.zh: 于是血糖开始升高。

cues.en: That's diabetes.
cues.zh: 这就是糖尿病。

cues.en: It probably won't surprise you to hear that most of my patients have insulin
cues.zh: 听到我的大多数患者都有胰岛素

cues.en: resistance or diabetes.
cues.zh: 抵抗或糖尿病，你可能不会感到意外。

cues.en: And if you're sitting there thinking, that's
cues.zh: 如果你坐在那里想，那

cues.en: not me, you actually might wanna think again because almost fifty percent of adult Americans now have diabetes or prediabetes.
cues.zh: 不是我，你其实可能要再想想，因为现在近百分之五十的美国成年人有糖尿病或糖尿病前期。

cues.en: That is almost a hundred and twenty million of us.
cues.zh: 那可是将近一亿两千万人。

cues.en: But that's hardly everyone who has issues with insulin.
cues.zh: 但这远不是所有有胰岛素问题的人。

cues.en: Because as I was saying, people have elevated insulin levels due to insulin resistance
cues.zh: 因为正如我所说，人们由于胰岛素抵抗而胰岛素水平升高

cues.en: for years,
cues.zh: 长达数年，

cues.en: even decades
cues.zh: 甚至数十年

cues.en: before the diagnosis of even prediabetes
cues.zh: 在甚至还没被诊断出糖尿病前期

cues.en: is made.
cues.zh: 之前。

cues.en: Plus, it's been shown that sixteen to twenty five percent of normal weight adults are also insulin resistant.
cues.zh: 此外，研究显示百分之十六到二十五的正常体重成年人也有胰岛素抵抗。

cues.en: So in case you're keeping track,
cues.zh: 所以如果你在算账的话，

cues.en: this is a heck of a lot of us.
cues.zh: 我们中这样的人可真是太多了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the trouble with insulin resistance is
cues.zh: 胰岛素抵抗的麻烦在于

cues.en: if it goes up,
cues.zh: 如果它升高，

cues.en: we are at great risk for developing type two diabetes.
cues.zh: 我们发展成二型糖尿病的风险就很大。

cues.en: But, also,
cues.zh: 但是，还有，

cues.en: insulin
cues.zh: 胰岛素

cues.en: makes us hungry,
cues.zh: 让我们感到饥饿，

cues.en: and the food we eat
cues.zh: 而我们吃的食物

cues.en: much more likely to be stored as fat.
cues.zh: 更容易被储存为脂肪。

cues.en: Insulin is our fat storage hormone.
cues.zh: 胰岛素是我们的脂肪储存激素。

cues.en: So we can start to see how it's gonna be a problem for diseases like obesity
cues.zh: 所以我们能开始看出，这对肥胖这类疾病

cues.en: and metabolic issues like diabetes.
cues.zh: 和糖尿病这类代谢问题来说，怎么会成为一个问题。

cues.en: But what if we trace this problem back to the beginning
cues.zh: 但如果我们把这个问题追溯到源头

cues.en: and we just didn't have so much glucose around that insulin needed to deal with. Let's take a look at how that could be.
cues.zh: 并且根本没有那么多葡萄糖需要胰岛素来处理呢？让我们看看那会是怎样。

cues.en: Everything you eat is either a carbohydrate,
cues.zh: 你吃的一切要么是碳水化合物、

cues.en: a protein, or a fat,
cues.zh: 要么是蛋白质、要么是脂肪，

cues.en: and they all have a very different effect on glucose and therefore insulin levels, as you can see on the graph.
cues.zh: 它们对葡萄糖以及因此对胰岛素水平的影响截然不同，正如你在图上看到的。

cues.en: So when we eat carbohydrates,
cues.zh: 所以当我们吃碳水化合物时，

cues.en: our insulin and glucose are gonna spike up fast.
cues.zh: 我们的胰岛素和葡萄糖会迅速飙升。

cues.en: And with proteins,
cues.zh: 而吃蛋白质时，

cues.en: it looks a lot better.
cues.zh: 情况看起来好多了。

cues.en: But take a look at what happens when we eat fat.
cues.zh: 但看看我们吃脂肪时会发生什么。

cues.en: Essentially
cues.zh: 基本上

cues.en: nothing,
cues.zh: 什么都没发生，

cues.en: a flat line.
cues.zh: 一条平线。

cues.en: And this is gonna wind up being very
cues.zh: 而这最终会变得非常

cues.en: important.
cues.zh: 重要。

cues.en: So now I wanna translate that graph for you into a real world situation.
cues.zh: 现在我想把那张图翻译成一个现实世界的场景。

cues.en: I want you to go back and think about the last time you ate an American version of Chinese food.
cues.zh: 我想让你回想一下你上次吃美式中餐的时候。

cues.en: We all know there's rules associated with this. Right? And the first rule is you're gonna overeat because the stop signal doesn't get sent until you are literally busting at the seams.
cues.zh: 我们都知道这有一些规律，对吧？第一条规律是你会吃撑，因为停止信号直到你真的撑到 seams 都裂开才会发出。

cues.en: Rule number two is in an hour, you're starving.
cues.zh: 第二条规律是一小时后你就饿得不行。

cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: Well, because the rice in that meal caused glucose and insulin to skyrocket,
cues.zh: 因为那顿饭里的米饭让葡萄糖和胰岛素飙升，

cues.en: which triggered hunger,
cues.zh: 从而触发了饥饿、

cues.en: fat storage, and cravings.
cues.zh: 脂肪储存和渴望。

cues.en: So if you're insulin resistant to begin with and your insulin levels are already higher,
cues.zh: 所以如果你本来就是胰岛素抵抗，而且你的胰岛素水平已经更高，

cues.en: you really are hungrier all the time. And we have this set up.
cues.zh: 你就真的会一直更饿。而我们就造成了这种局面。

cues.en: Eat carbs, your glucose goes up, your insulin goes up, and you have hunger and fat storage.
cues.zh: 吃碳水，血糖升高，胰岛素升高，然后你就会感到饥饿并储存脂肪。

cues.en: So how do we recommend to these people to eat?
cues.zh: 那我们该怎么建议这些人吃呢？

cues.en: Because it seems like that would be really important,
cues.zh: 因为这看起来非常重要，

cues.en: and it is.
cues.zh: 确实如此。

cues.en: Let's focus just on type two diabetes
cues.zh: 我们先聚焦二型糖尿病，

cues.en: because the general recommendations
cues.zh: 因为一般的建议

cues.en: are to tell patients with type two diabetes to consume
cues.zh: 是告诉二型糖尿病患者

cues.en: 40 to 65 grams of carbohydrates
cues.zh: 每餐摄入40到65克碳水，

cues.en: per meal plus more at snacks.
cues.zh: 零食还要再加。

cues.en: Trust me on this. That's a lot of carbs.
cues.zh: 相信我，这碳水可不少。

cues.en: And remember what's gonna happen to glucose and insulin, blood sugar and insulin, when we eat them?
cues.zh: 还记得我们吃下它们后，血糖和胰岛素会发生什么吗？

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: We are essentially recommending
cues.zh: 我们实际上是在建议

cues.en: that they eat exactly what's
cues.zh: 他们吃的正是

cues.en: causing their problem.
cues.zh: 导致他们问题的东西。

cues.en: Sound crazy?
cues.zh: 听起来很疯狂吧？

cues.en: It really, really is.
cues.zh: 真的，真的非常疯狂。

cues.en: Because at its root, diabetes is a state of carbohydrate
cues.zh: 因为从根本上说，糖尿病就是一种碳水

cues.en: toxicity.
cues.zh: 中毒状态。

cues.en: We can't get the blood sugar into the cells, and that causes a problem in the short term, but the long term consequences
cues.zh: 血糖进不了细胞，短期内就造成问题，但长期后果

cues.en: are even greater.
cues.zh: 更加严重。

cues.en: And insulin resistance is essentially a state of carbohydrate
cues.zh: 而胰岛素抵抗本质上就是一种碳水

cues.en: intolerance.
cues.zh: 不耐受。

cues.en: So why, oh, why do we wanna continue to recommend to people to eat them?
cues.zh: 那我们究竟为什么还要继续建议人们吃碳水呢？

cues.en: The American Diabetes Association guidelines
cues.zh: 美国糖尿病协会的指南

cues.en: specifically state that there is inconclusive
cues.zh: 明确指出，目前没有确凿

cues.en: evidence to recommend a specific carbohydrate limit,
cues.zh: 证据来推荐具体的碳水摄入上限，

cues.en: but those guidelines go right on to say what we all know.
cues.zh: 但指南紧接着又说出了我们都知道的事实。

cues.en: Carbohydrate intake is the single biggest factor in blood sugar levels and, therefore,
cues.zh: 碳水摄入是影响血糖水平的唯一最大因素，因此

cues.en: need for medication.
cues.zh: 也决定了用药需求。

cues.en: These guidelines then go on to say, hey. Look. If you're taking certain diabetic medications,
cues.zh: 指南接着还说，嘿，注意。如果你在服用某些糖尿病药物，

cues.en: you actually have to eat carbs. Other... Otherwise, your blood sugar can go too low.
cues.zh: 你其实必须吃碳水。否则……否则你的血糖会降得太低。

cues.en: Okay. So let's take a look at the vicious cycle that that advice just set up. So it's eat carbs,
cues.zh: 好，那我们来看看这条建议带来的恶性循环。就是吃碳水，

cues.en: so you have to take medicine.
cues.zh: 然后你就得吃药。

cues.en: Then you have to eat more carbs so you avoid the side effect of those medications,
cues.zh: 接着你得吃更多碳水，来避免那些药物的副作用，

cues.en: and around and around we go.
cues.zh: 然后就这样循环往复。

cues.en: Even worse is that nowhere in the ADA guidelines
cues.zh: 更糟的是，ADA指南里压根儿就没有

cues.en: is the goal of reversing type two diabetes.
cues.zh: 逆转二型糖尿病这个目标。

cues.en: This needs to be changed because type two diabetes
cues.zh: 这必须改变，因为二型糖尿病

cues.en: can be reversed
cues.zh: 是可以逆转的，

cues.en: in many, if not most situations,
cues.zh: 在很多情况下，甚至大多数情况下，

cues.en: especially if we start early.
cues.zh: 尤其是如果我们尽早开始。

cues.en: Not only do we need to let people know this, but we have to start giving them the practical advice
cues.zh: 我们不仅要让人们知道这一点，还得开始给他们实用的建议，

cues.en: so they can do this.
cues.zh: 让他们能够做到。

cues.en: Consider carbs.
cues.zh: 说说碳水。

cues.en: First, here's a shocker for you. We don't need them.
cues.zh: 首先，给你个震撼的事实：我们根本不需要它。

cues.en: Seriously.
cues.zh: 说真的。

cues.en: Our minimum daily requirement for carbohydrates is zero.
cues.zh: 我们每天对碳水的最低需求量是零。

cues.en: We have essential amino acids,
cues.zh: 我们有必需氨基酸，

cues.en: those are proteins, essential fatty acids, but nope, no essential carb.
cues.zh: 那是蛋白质，还有必需脂肪酸，但没有，没有必需碳水。

cues.en: A nutrient is essential if
cues.zh: 一种营养素之所以是必需的，前提是

cues.en: we have to have it to function,
cues.zh: 我们必须靠它来维持机能，

cues.en: and we can't make it from something else.
cues.zh: 而且无法从其他东西合成。

cues.en: We make glucose, plenty of it, all the time. It's called gluconeogenesis.
cues.zh: 我们会合成葡萄糖，大量的，一直都在。这叫糖异生。

cues.en: So we don't need them.
cues.zh: 所以我们不需要它。

cues.en: The overconsumption of them is making us very sick, yet we are continuing to recommend to patients to consume close to, if not more, than half of their total energy intake every day from them?
cues.zh: 过量摄入碳水让我们病得很重，可我们却还在建议患者每天从碳水里摄入接近、甚至超过一半的总能量？

cues.en: It doesn't make sense.
cues.zh: 这说不通。

cues.en: Let's talk about what does.
cues.zh: 来说说什么才说得通。

cues.en: Cutting carbs a lot. Yes. In my clinic, we teach patients to eat with carbs as the minority of their intake,
cues.zh: 大幅减少碳水。没错。在我的诊所里，我们教患者把碳水作为摄入的少数，

cues.en: not the majority.
cues.zh: 而不是多数。

cues.en: So how does that work?
cues.zh: 那它是怎么运作的呢？

cues.en: Well, when our patients decrease their carbs, their glucose goes down, and they don't need as much insulin.
cues.zh: 好的，当我们的患者减少碳水化合物摄入时，他们的血糖会下降，也就不需要那么多胰岛素了。

cues.en: So those insulin levels drop and fast.
cues.zh: 所以胰岛素水平会迅速下降。

cues.en: And this is very important because a study looking at our National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data, better known as NHANES,
cues.zh: 这非常重要，因为一项研究分析了我们的国家健康与营养调查数据，也就是大家熟知的 NHANES，

cues.en: showed that the single biggest risk factor for coronary artery disease is insulin resistance.
cues.zh: 表明，冠状动脉疾病最大的风险因素就是胰岛素抵抗。

cues.en: It is responsible for a whopping forty two percent of heart attacks.
cues.zh: 它导致了高达百分之四十二的心脏病发作。

cues.en: Low carb intervention works so fast that we can literally pull people off of hundreds of units of insulin in days to weeks.
cues.zh: 低碳干预见效极快，我们甚至能在几天到几周内，让患者彻底停用几百个单位的胰岛素。

cues.en: One of my favorite stories is a very recent one. A young gal, but who had an almost twenty year history of type two diabetes,
cues.zh: 我最喜欢的故事之一就发生在最近。一位年轻姑娘，却有近二十年的2型糖尿病病史，

cues.en: came in when a physician from another clinic told her she was just sick and should probably get used to it. Her diabetes was way out of control. This despite the fact that she was on multiple medications,
cues.zh: 一位来自另一家诊所的医生告诉她，她只是生病了，可能得习惯这种情况。她的糖尿病完全失控了。尽管她正在服用多种药物，

cues.en: including
cues.zh: 包括

cues.en: almost three hundred units of insulin
cues.zh: 将近三百个单位的胰岛素

cues.en: that was being injected into her continuously
cues.zh: 它被持续注入到她体内

cues.en: every day via a pump. All of this, remember, blood sugar's still out of control.
cues.zh: 每天靠泵来维持。记住，这一切发生时，血糖仍然失控。

cues.en: So we put her on a low carb diet, and now let's fast forward four months. She lost weight, yes, but better than that,
cues.zh: 于是我们让她采用低碳水饮食，现在快进四个月。她确实瘦了，但更重要的是，

cues.en: sick no more. Her blood sugar levels were now normal all of the time.
cues.zh: 病愈了，不再受病痛折磨。她的血糖水平现在一直保持正常。

cues.en: This on, get this,
cues.zh: 这个开着，听听这个，

cues.en: no diabetes medication.
cues.zh: 不服用糖尿病药物。

cues.en: Gone was the three hundred units of insulin.
cues.zh: 300个单位的胰岛素，不用打了。

cues.en: No more insulin pump. No more pricking her finger multiple times each day. Gone. All of it. No more diabetes.
cues.zh: 不用再带胰岛素泵，不用再每天扎好几次手指。都没了，全摆脱了。糖尿病没了。

cues.en: One of the greatest joys of my job is to be able to tell a patient like this that they no longer have diabetes,
cues.zh: 我工作中最开心的时刻之一，就是能告诉这样的患者他们不再有糖尿病了，

cues.en: and we ceremoniously take it off their problem list together. So are they cured? Is this a miracle?
cues.zh: 然后一起郑重地把它从病历清单里划掉。那他们算治愈了吗？这是奇迹吗？

cues.en: We'll leave that grandstanding to doctor Oz.
cues.zh: 这种博人眼球的噱头还是留给 Doctor Oz 吧。

cues.en: Cured would imply that it can't come back. And if they start eating excessive carbs again, it will. So no. Not cured.
cues.zh: “治愈”意味着不会复发。可如果他们重新摄入过量碳水，病情就会卷土重来。所以并没有治愈。

cues.en: But they don't have diabetes any longer. It's resolved,
cues.zh: 但他们确实不再有糖尿病了。病情缓解了，

cues.en: and it can stay that way as long as we keep away the cause.
cues.zh: 只要远离病因，就能一直保持下去。

cues.en: So what does this look like then? How does somebody eat this way? Well, first, let me tell you what it's not. Low carb is not zero carb, and it is not
cues.zh: 那这具体是怎样的呢？到底该怎么吃？首先，我先讲讲它不是什么。低碳不是零碳，也不是

cues.en: high protein.
cues.zh: 高蛋白。

cues.en: These are common criticisms that are so frustrating because they're not true.
cues.zh: 这些都是常见的质疑，很让人无奈，因为事实根本不是这样。

cues.en: Next, if we take the carbs out, what are we gonna put in? Because remember, there's only three macronutrients.
cues.zh: 接着，如果我们减掉了碳水，那该补充什么？别忘了，宏量营养素只有三种。

cues.en: If one goes down, one has to go up.
cues.zh: 一种减少了，另一种就必须增加。

cues.en: My patients eat fat and a lot of it.
cues.zh: 我的患者会吃脂肪，而且是吃大量的脂肪。

cues.en: What, you say? I mean, what's going to happen when you eat fat?
cues.zh: 你可能会说：什么？吃脂肪会怎么样？

cues.en: Well, let me tell you. You're going to be happy because fat tastes great, and it is incredibly satisfying.
cues.zh: 我来告诉你吧。你会很开心，因为脂肪不仅美味，还极具饱腹感。

cues.en: But remember,
cues.zh: 但更重要的是，

cues.en: fat is the only macronutrient
cues.zh: 脂肪是唯一一种

cues.en: that's gonna keep our glucose, blood sugar, and insulin levels low, and that is so
cues.zh: 能让葡萄糖、血糖和胰岛素水平维持在低位的宏量营养素，而这

cues.en: important.
cues.zh: 至关重要。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I want you to now hear my simple rules for eating. These rules, you have to remember, are even gonna be more important if you are one of the tens of millions of Americans
cues.zh: 现在我想让你们听听我的简单饮食规则。要记住，这些规则对几千万美国人中的一员来说更为重要

cues.en: who have trouble with insulin levels. Rule number one, if it says light, low fat, or fat free, stays in the grocery store. Because if they took the fat out, they put carbs and chemicals in. Rule number two, eat food.
cues.zh: 这些人有胰岛素水平问题。第一条规则，如果标着轻食、低脂或零脂，就留在杂货店里。因为他们把脂肪拿掉了，就会放进去碳水和化学物质。第二条规则，吃食物。

cues.en: The most important rule in low carb nutrition,
cues.zh: 低碳水营养最重要的规则，

cues.en: Real food does not come in a box, and no one should have to tell you real food is natural. You should know that when you look at it.
cues.zh: 真正的食物不会装在盒子里，而且不应该需要别人告诉你真正的食物是天然的。你看到它的时候就应该知道。

cues.en: Don't eat anything you don't like.
cues.zh: 不要吃任何你不喜欢的东西。

cues.en: And eat when you're hungry. Don't eat when you're not, no matter what the clock says.
cues.zh: 饿了就吃。不饿就别吃，不管钟表上显示几点。

cues.en: And number five is a simple way to remember what we want to avoid. No GPS.
cues.zh: 第五条是一个简单的方法，帮你记住我们要避免什么。不要GPS。

cues.en: No grains,
cues.zh: 不要谷物，

cues.en: no potatoes,
cues.zh: 不要土豆，

cues.en: and no sugar.
cues.zh: 不要糖。

cues.en: That last one is a biggie. Right? No grains? Yeah. No grains. But we have to have them. Nope. They're a carb. But whole grains are so good for us. Well, first of all, there are actually very few foods out there that are truly whole grain even when they say they are. Most foods that purport themselves to be whole grain are highly processed and the fiber benefit ruined,
cues.zh: 最后一条是大问题。对吧？不要谷物？对。不要谷物。可我们必须吃谷物啊。不。它们是碳水。但全谷物对我们太好了。首先，实际上真正是全谷物的食物非常少，即使它们声称是。大多数自称全谷物的食物都经过高度加工，纤维的好处被破坏了，

cues.en: or they're coming with highly refined flour,
cues.zh: 或者它们带着高度精制的面粉，

cues.en: usually both of these things. So if you are one of the truly insulin sensitive people, you can eat real whole grain. But if you are in the enormous slice of our population with insulin issues, it's making things worse.
cues.zh: 通常是这两种情况都有。所以如果你是真正胰岛素敏感的人，你可以吃真正的全谷物。但如果你属于我们人口中胰岛素问题庞大的那一部分，它会让情况更糟。

cues.en: So what if you are one of the real insulin sensitive people? Can you still eat this way? Yes.
cues.zh: 那如果你是真正胰岛素敏感的人之一呢？还能这样吃吗？可以。

cues.en: I'm a great example.
cues.zh: 我就是个好例子。

cues.en: Over a year ago, I decided I would cut my carbs as low as I recommend to my diabetic patients. Now it's not mandatory for my health like it is for theirs.
cues.zh: 一年多以前，我决定把碳水降到跟我推荐给糖尿病患者的水平一样低。不过这对我的健康来说不是必须的，不像他们那样。

cues.en: I'm not insulin resistant, so would this be a problem? No. That's just the thing. Unless you have an exceedingly rare syndrome, then cutting carbs is gonna be good for you even if it's not necessary.
cues.zh: 我没有胰岛素抵抗，所以这会有问题吗？不会。这正是关键所在。除非你患有一种极其罕见的综合征，否则减少碳水对你是件好事，即使它不是必需的。

cues.en: I wanna show you a couple pictures of my radical food.
cues.zh: 我想给你看几张我日常食物的照片。

cues.en: So this is a common breakfast in my house. So does it look like I just broke my own rule? I didn't because this muffin is made with coconut flour. I bake all the time still. I just use non grain based flours.
cues.zh: 这是我家常见的早餐。看起来像是我刚打破了自己的规则？并没有，因为这个松饼是用椰子粉做的。我仍然经常烘焙。我只是用非谷物类的粉。

cues.en: Coconut, almond, hazelnut, flax, they make delicious things. And this is a typical dinner in my house with a typical starch.
cues.zh: 椰子、杏仁、榛子、亚麻，它们能做出美味的东西。这是我家典型的晚餐，配一个典型的淀粉类食物。

cues.en: That would be the sauteed mushrooms.
cues.zh: 那就是炒蘑菇。

cues.en: Now my patients and I eat delightful food all of the time and enjoy it. But what about the research on this? I mean, is this just anecdotal evidence now from my clinic? No.
cues.zh: 现在我和我的患者一直都在吃美味的食物并享受其中。但关于这方面的研究呢？我是说，这些现在只是我诊所的轶事证据吗？不是。

cues.en: There are dozens of randomized controlled trials looking at low carb intervention for things like diabetes,
cues.zh: 有几十项随机对照试验在研究低碳水干预对糖尿病等疾病的作用，

cues.en: cardiovascular risk factors, obesity,
cues.zh: 心血管风险因素、肥胖，

cues.en: they're consistent. It works.
cues.zh: 结果是一致的。它有效。

cues.en: There are even a large numbers, number of studies showing that low carb nutrition decreases inflammatory
cues.zh: 甚至有大量研究表明，低碳水营养能降低炎症

cues.en: markers, which is making it really exciting for diseases like cancer.
cues.zh: 标志物，这让它在癌症等疾病方面非常令人兴奋。

cues.en: We just finished a study in our clinic, and what we did is we took 50 type two diabetic patients that were treated with our low carb, high fat based program,
cues.zh: 我们刚在诊所完成了一项研究，我们选取了50名2型糖尿病患者，采用我们的低碳水、高脂肪方案进行治疗，

cues.en: and we compared them to 50 patients who were treated with the ADA guidelines.
cues.zh: 我们将他们与 50 位按照 ADA 指南治疗的患者进行了对比。

cues.en: And after six months, not only did we find a significant metabolic advantage for the low carb group, but, and let's face it, this is important,
cues.zh: 六个月后，我们不仅发现低碳水化合物组有明显的代谢优势，而且，说实话，这一点很重要，

cues.en: a huge cost savings.
cues.zh: 巨大的成本节省。

cues.en: Our analysis showed that our patients could save over $2,000
cues.zh: 我们的分析显示，患者可节省超过2000美元

cues.en: a year just
cues.zh: 一年刚刚

cues.en: on the diabetes meds they were no longer taking. Just think how fast that adds up in our diabetes epidemic now that we are spending $250,000,000,000
cues.zh: 他们不再服用的糖尿病药物。想想在我们如今的糖尿病流行中，这积累得有多快，我们每年要花2500亿美元

cues.en: a year on in this country.
cues.zh: 在这个国家待了一年。

cues.en: So I wanna show you a slide now that demonstrate... Where demonstrates where that savings is coming from.
cues.zh: 现在我想给你们看一张幻灯片，展示……展示这些节省是从哪里来的。

cues.en: So this is looking just at the insulin difference in the two groups after six months, and what we can see is that the low carb group was able to decrease their insulin by almost 500,
cues.zh: 这里只看六个月后两组之间的胰岛素差异，我们可以看到，低碳水组能把胰岛素降低近500，

cues.en: whereas in the ADA treated group, they had to increase their insulin by almost three hundred and fifty units a day. Two important things. Number one,
cues.zh: 而在 ADA 治疗组中，他们每天必须增加近 350 个单位的胰岛素。这里有两点很重要。第一，

cues.en: insulin's expensive.
cues.zh: 胰岛素很贵。

cues.en: And number two, not all the people in this study were even on insulin,
cues.zh: 第二点，这项研究中甚至不是所有人都用了胰岛素，

cues.en: which makes these results even more impressive.
cues.zh: 这让这些结果更加令人印象深刻。

cues.en: But what I would say is that this graph really represents
cues.zh: 但我想说的是，这张图真正展现的是

cues.en: two different approaches to treating this disease.
cues.zh: 治疗这种疾病有两种不同的方法。

cues.en: The first,
cues.zh: 第一组，

cues.en: our group with the goal of reversing disease, meaning they need less medicine. And the second group, which very clearly aligns with the ADA guidelines,
cues.zh: 我们团队的目标是逆转疾病，意味着他们需要更少的药物。而第二组，则非常明确地符合ADA指南，

cues.en: which states that diabetes
cues.zh: 该指南指出糖尿病

cues.en: is a progressive disease requiring more medicine over time. Progressive
cues.zh: 是一种渐进性疾病，随着时间推移需要更多药物。是渐进性的，

cues.en: unless we take away the cause.
cues.zh: 除非我们消除病因。

cues.en: So what's the problem then? Why is this not everywhere? Why isn't low carb the norm? There's two big reasons. Number one, status quo. It is hard to break.
cues.zh: 那么问题出在哪里？为什么这种方法没有普及？为什么低碳水饮食没有成为常态？有两个主要原因。第一，现状难以打破。

cues.en: There are many agendas involved.
cues.zh: 其中涉及许多利益考量。

cues.en: We got this notion that low fat was the way to go decades ago, but a recent study just came out showing that there was zero randomized control evidence to recommend to Americans to remove the fat from our diet, and that's how the carbs got added in. It was essentially
cues.zh: 几十年前我们形成了低脂饮食是正确方向的观念，但最近一项研究表明，没有任何随机对照证据支持建议美国人从饮食中去除脂肪，而碳水化合物正是这样被加入的。这本质上

cues.en: a huge experiment
cues.zh: 是一个巨大的实验

cues.en: on millions of people, and it failed
cues.zh: 涉及数百万人，结果却

cues.en: miserably.
cues.zh: 惨败。

cues.en: The second reason we don't see it everywhere is money.
cues.zh: 我们没能普及低碳水饮食的第二个原因是金钱。

cues.en: Don't be fooled. There's a lot of money to be made from keeping you sick. And what we see is with these specialty guideline panels, they are stacked with conflict of interest.
cues.zh: 别被蒙蔽了。让你保持生病状态可以赚很多钱。我们看到这些专业指南专家组中充斥着利益冲突。

cues.en: So the solution to the diabetes epidemic in my clinic is exceedingly
cues.zh: 所以在我诊所里，解决糖尿病流行病的方法非常

cues.en: clear.
cues.zh: 明确。

cues.en: Stop
cues.zh: 停止

cues.en: using medicine
cues.zh: 用药物

cues.en: to treat food.
cues.zh: 来对付食物。

cues.en: And for a disease whose root cause is carbohydrates,
cues.zh: 对于一种根本原因是碳水化合物的疾病，

cues.en: take away the carbohydrates
cues.zh: 去除碳水化合物

cues.en: or at least cut them so we can remember what we used to know.
cues.zh: 或者至少减少它们，让我们重新记起曾经知道的东西。

cues.en: We knew it a long time ago. This was said thousands of years ago, and we need, in this day and age, to get back to that notion.
cues.zh: 我们很久以前就知道这一点。这是几千年前就说过的话，在这个时代，我们需要回归那个理念。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
